newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FORECAST - Swiss banks stick to Q1 GDP forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swiss banks stick to Q1 GDP forecasts.

text.p: Most Swiss banks surveyed in mid-May have not changed their outlook for Swiss first quarter gross domestic product data, to be released on Thursday.
The data are expected by 0600 GMT.

Averaged on the basis of a survey of five banks, Swiss first quarter GDP, annualised and seasonally adjusted, is expected to show a 0.3 percent increase versus fourth quarter 1996, unchanged from a similar forecast made in mid-May.

Compared with the first quarter 1996, first quarter 1997 is now expected to show a less pronounced drop of 0.3 percent versus an earlier average forecast for a 0.4 percent decline, due to a slight upward revision by one bank.
One economist saw a danger the data would be weaker than expected, but some others believed they could be slightly higher than anticipated.

"I think a lot of people are quite confused regarding Switzerland. It remains to be seen whether something is finally starting to improve. I think consumption is slowly, slowly beginning to pick up," said one economist.
Swiss retail sales for April reported on June 2 showed a 2.0 percent increase from the previous year, but the rise reflected two additional shopping days.

Another economist saw a chance the numbers would be lower than expected, noting Swiss trade data, building and investment activities were weak or negative in the first quarter. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
